ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, you know? (Kokoro wa, nanika ga arimasu)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, and each node is trying to figure out patterns in the data. It's like a big game of "connect the dots," but with lots of math and algorithms. (Sūshin to, kōryū no kōryū)

But here's the thing: even the creators can't fully predict what the network will do, even with all the data and math they throw at it. It's like trying to predict a random number generator, (Rando nāmabā jōgenjō)

or even a human's thought process. It's all very mysterious, and that's what makes these networks so powerful. (Mystery to, tsukamu)

So, when people say that the creators don't fully understand how these networks work, they mean that it's like trying to grasp a handful of sand – the more you try to hold onto it, the more it slips away. (Kokoro o tsukamu, kūki no kūki)

It's a complex, intricate system that's still being studied and improved, but for now, it's a bit like magic. (Mahō to, tsukamu)
